ours-poly.short: Night School's curve fits, computed for this film
ours-poly.citation: media/school/heldout/facts.json (poly section), written by tools/school/fill_heldout.mjs from system/school/heldout.mjs: least squares by Householder QR; ridge by QR on the design matrix stacked over sqrt(lambda) times the identity.
claims: 16 training points from sin(pi x) with noise sigma 0.2; 500 held-out points. Degree 3 held-out RMSE 0.330; degree 15 train RMSE 1.4e-11 and held-out RMSE 3,936.
Ridge at degree 15: held-out RMSE 3,936 at lambda 0, 0.429 at 0.01 (the best of 7), 0.703 at 100.
Over 200 training draws, degree 3 is the best degree on held-out data 113 times.

Degree 3 and the penalty 0.01 were picked on the same held-out points they are scored on, which flatters them a little. The wild curve's held-out error is 2.99 on points inside the training range and far larger past the outermost training points.
ours-poly.n: 16 training and 500 held-out points; 200 draws for the spread.
ours-poly.interval: 5th to 95th percentiles over 200 draws are in facts.json.
ours-poly.does_not_prove: Anything about real data; a toy curve chosen to show one effect.

goodfellow2016.short: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville 2016, Deep Learning
goodfellow2016.citation: Goodfellow, I., Bengio, Y., Courville, A. (2016). Deep Learning. MIT Press. Chapter 5.2 (capacity, overfitting and underfitting) and 5.3 (hyperparameters and validation sets).
claims: Training error falls as capacity grows, while test error typically falls and then rises (overfitting).
Choosing hyperparameters on the test set biases it; a separate validation set is used for choices, and the test set only to estimate generalisation at the end.

hoerl1970.citation: Hoerl, A. E., Kennard, R. W. (1970). Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems. Technometrics 12(1), 55-67.
claims: Ridge regression adds a penalty on the size of the coefficients (lambda times their sum of squares) to least squares.

ours-spiral.short: Night School's spiral network on 40 points against 400
ours-spiral.citation: media/school/heldout/facts.json (spiral section): the F4 network, plain descent at 0.3, 10,000 updates, on the first 40 of the 400 training points and, as the control, on all 400.
claims: Both reach training accuracy 1. Held-out accuracy 0.7825 with 40 points, 0.995 with 400. With 40 points the held-out loss is lowest at update 300 (0.648) and ends at 1.487.
Over five different 40-point draws, held-out accuracy ranges from 0.755 to 0.86.
After the held-out loss minimum at update 300, held-out accuracy still rises, to 0.8025 at update 1,000, while the held-out loss climbs.
ours-spiral.does_not_prove: Anything general about how many points a task needs.

ours-model.short: Night School's tiny transformer, its training and held-out losses
ours-model.citation: media/school/heldout/facts.json (attention section): model.json's own curves, and the final weights rescored on rows they were trained on, on unseen rows of the same stream, on the lab's 256 held-out rows and on five fresh 256-row draws.
claims: The trainer draws a fresh batch every update; the generator repeats rows by chance: 507 of the 32,000 training rows were exact copies of earlier rows, and no row came round more than 5 times. 8 of the 256 'unseen' rows and 3 of the lab's 256 held-out rows also occur in training (facts.json, attention.repeats).
Final weights: loss 0.626 on the last 16 trained batches, 0.668 on the next 16 unseen batches, 0.687 on the lab's held-out rows, 0.650 to 0.672 on five fresh draws.
ours-model.n: 256 rows per score; five fresh draws.
ours-model.does_not_prove: That the model would not memorise with repeated data; it never had any.
